# 1\. LAB OVERVIEW

## 1.1  Why This Lab Exists

On AWS the numbers behind an SLO live in CloudWatch: request counts and error counts from a load balancer or an application, and the logs that explain them. An SLI is a ratio of good events to valid events; the SLO is the target; the error budget is what you may fail; the burn rate tells you how fast the budget is being used right now.

In this lab you deploy a small shop stack (one EC2 instance with an EBS data volume) from a CloudFormation template. It publishes checkout metrics and writes an application log. A checkout incident repeats every 30 minutes (:20–:24 and :50–:54 UTC) and the last three hours of history are already there. You graph the incident, calculate the error ratio and burn rate with metric math, create a burn alarm, cross-check the count in Logs Insights and then use 28 days of history to calculate the error budget and recommend a release decision.

| 🎯  NIIT iRUN Alignment |
| :---- |
| INCIDENT OWNERSHIP: You can turn a failure in CloudWatch into a number the product owner understands: error ratio, burn rate and budget left. |
| TROUBLESHOOTING EXCELLENCE: You check a metric against the logs before you report it. |
| OPERATIONAL READINESS: You decide release, careful release or freeze from the error budget, not from a feeling. |

## 1.2  Lab Scenario

| 📢  Incident Briefing — Can We Release This Week? |
| :---- |
| TIME: 11:00 │ PRIORITY: MEDIUM │ ASSIGNED TO: You |
| REQUEST RECEIVED: "Checkout failed again for a few minutes. Did we break our 99.5 % reliability target, how much error budget is left, and can we ship the new release on Friday?" |
| CONTEXT: The checkout service writes Errors5xx and RequestCount to CloudWatch (namespace ShopLab2/\<seat\>, dimension Service \= checkout) and JSON log lines to the log group /shop/\<seat\>/lab2/app. Twenty-eight days of daily totals are in data/sli-history.csv, the incident list in data/incidents.csv. |
| YOUR MISSION: Deploy the stack, measure the SLI and burn rate of the incident, create an alarm, confirm the numbers in the logs, calculate the 28-day error budget and recommend a release decision. You have 28 minutes for the core tasks. |

*Figure: Day 6 Lab 2 — Starting Environment: AWS Console in Your Sandbox Account (One Region); Stack Not Yet Created; CloudFormation, CloudWatch Metrics, Logs Insights and CloudShell Open in Separate Tabs*

## 1.3  Conceptual Foundation

The SLI, SLO, error budget and burn rate are connected by simple arithmetic. With a 99.5 % SLO the error budget is 0.5 %.

*Figure: SLI → SLO → Error Budget → Burn Rate — SLI \= 1 − Errors5xx / RequestCount · Budget \= 1 − SLO · Burn Rate \= Error Ratio ÷ Budget (1 \= exactly on budget)*

| Term | Meaning | In This Lab | Typical Question |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| SLI | Good events ÷ valid events | 1 − Errors5xx / RequestCount | How reliable were we? |
| SLO | Target for the SLI over a window | 99.5 % over 28 days | Is the target met? |
| Error budget | 1 − SLO, in events | RequestCount × 0.005 | How much may fail? |
| Burn rate | Error ratio ÷ budget ratio | Error % ÷ 0.5 | How fast are we using it? |

## 1.4  Learning Objectives

• Deploy a metric- and log-emitting EC2 stack from a CloudFormation template in the console

• Graph CloudWatch custom metrics with the Sum statistic and a 1-minute period in UTC

• Use metric math for the error ratio and the burn rate

• Create a CloudWatch alarm on a metric-math expression

• Cross-check a metric with a CloudWatch Logs Insights query

• Calculate a 28-day error budget and operational KPIs (MTTD, MTTR) and recommend a release decision

# 3\. CONCEPT DEEP-DIVE BEFORE STARTING

## 3.1  Metric Math and Burn Rate

In CloudWatch, metric math lets you combine metrics with an expression. Label the metrics m1 \= Errors5xx and m2 \= RequestCount, both with the statistic **Sum**; then 100 \* m1 / m2 is the error percentage and (m1 / m2) / 0.005 is the burn rate for a 99.5 % SLO. A burn rate of 1 uses the budget exactly over the whole window; 14.4 for one hour uses 2 % of a 30-day budget.

| 💡  Why This Matters Operationally |
| :---- |
| The 28-day SLI moves slowly, so a 5-minute outage barely changes it. The burn rate over a short window shows at once that the budget is being spent, and that is what you alarm on. |

## 3.2  The Critical Distinction: Sum vs Average and Period

Counts must be added up (Sum) per period. Average of a count gives requests per sample, not the total, and a period of 5 minutes shows the total of five 1-minute values. Always set the **time zone to UTC** so the incident minutes (:20–:24) match the log lines.

| ⚠️  Most Common Mistake With CloudWatch Math |
| :---- |
| Using Average instead of Sum, or mixing periods (m1 at 1 minute, m2 at 5 minutes). Both metrics in an expression must use the same statistic and period. |

## 3.3  Settings You Need

| Setting | Value in This Lab | Why |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Namespace | ShopLab2/\<seat\> | Your own metrics only |
| Dimension | Service \= checkout | Select it for both metrics |
| Statistic / Period | Sum / 1 minute (5 minutes for the incident total) | Counts |
| Time zone | UTC | Matches the log timestamps |
| Alarm threshold | 7.2 (% error ratio) | Burn 14.4 × 0.5 % |

| **2.A Record the first bad minute, the failed requests, the error percentage and the burn rate of the incident.**  Answer: First bad minute :20 (and :50 for the second incident). Failed requests 392 out of 492, error ratio 79.7 %, burn rate ≈ 159\. |
| **2.B A burn rate of about 160 means what for a 28-day budget if it continued?**  Answer: The whole 28-day budget would be gone in 28 days ÷ 160 ≈ 4 hours. That is why a burn alarm pages long before the 28-day SLI moves. |

| **📟  Expected Output** |
| Availability SLI 99.7710 % · objective 99.50 % · bad 9,102 of 3,974,059 · budget 19,870 · consumed 45.8 % · remaining 54.2 % · MET |
| Latency\<0.5s SLI 99.6585 % · consumed 34.2 % · MET |
| Worst days: 2026-10-15 22.6 % · 2026-10-04 9.7 % · 2026-10-22 5.0 % of the budget |
| Operational KPIs: incidents 3 · MTTD 6.7 min · MTTR 33.7 min · incident share of budget 36.0 % |
| With 99.9 %: budget 3,974 · consumed 229.0 % · MISSED |
| **4.A Show the budget calculation by hand and name the incident that used the most budget.**  Answer: Total requests 3,974,059 × 0.005 \= about 19,870 failures allowed; actual failures 9,102; consumed 9,102 ÷ 19,870 \= 45.8 %. INC-4088 (PSP outage, no failover) used the most: 4,400 bad requests. |
| **4.B The same month is MET at 99.5 % and MISSED at 99.9 %. Who should choose the objective and on what basis?**  Answer: Product and engineering together, based on user expectations, business impact, the cost of reaching the target and the historical reliability; not 100 %. |
| **4.C Recommend release, careful release or freeze and why, in two sentences for a product owner.**  Answer: Careful release: the 28-day target is met but 45.8 % of the budget is already used and one more outage like INC-4088 would nearly exhaust it. Ship small, low-risk changes and watch the burn alarm. |

# 6\. TROUBLESHOOTING — COMMON ISSUES & FIXES

| Issue / Error | Cause | Diagnosis | Fix |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Stack fails: IAM capabilities | Capabilities box not ticked | Events tab of the stack | Tick the acknowledgement and retry |
| No ShopLab2/\<seat\> namespace | Instance still starting | EC2 status checks | Wait 5 minutes after CREATE\_COMPLETE; tell the instructor after 15 |
| Graph empty | Wrong statistic, period or time zone | Graphed metrics tab | Sum, 1 minute, UTC, last 3 hours |
| Access denied | Wrong region or a name without your seat id | Top-right region | Use the allowed region; start names with your seat id |
| Logs Insights returns nothing | Wrong log group or time range | Log group name | Select /shop/\<seat\>/lab2/app and a range with :20-:24 |
| CloudShell not available | Region or policy | Console message | Run the report on your laptop with python3 |

# 7\. INSTRUCTOR DEBRIEF — 7 MINUTES

## 7.1  Discussion Questions

| Discussion 1 — One Number, Three Views |
| :---- |
| What do the metric, the log count and the 28-day SLI each tell you? |
| Why must the metric and the log count agree? |
| Key insight: Trust in the SLI depends on cross-checks; the burn rate shows the present, the 28-day SLI the history. |

| Discussion 2 — Release Decision |
| :---- |
| Why careful release and not freeze? |
| What would make you freeze? |
| Key insight: The decision comes from the budget left: plenty → release; about half → careful; exhausted → freeze. |

## 7.2  Common Mistakes — Learn From These

| Mistake | Why It Happens | Consequence | Prevention |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Average instead of Sum | Default statistic | Wrong ratio | Sum for counts |
| Mixed periods in math | Metrics added separately | Empty or wrong result | Same period for both |
| Local time zone | Console default | Wrong minutes | Use UTC |
| Reading only the 28-day SLI | It looks fine | Misses fast burn | Alarm on burn rate |

1\. One sandbox AWS account (never production) and ONE allowed region. Learners need a default VPC in that region (the template uses the default subnet).

2\. IAM: create users u01–u40 (user name \= seat id) and attach INSTRUCTOR-learner-iam-policy.json (replace REGION and ACCOUNT\_ID). It allows CloudFormation, EC2, IAM roles for the stack, alarm and log access only for names with the seat id, and denies other regions.

4\. UNVERIFIED: the template, the user-data script, the CloudWatch agent timestamp handling, the IAM policy and the CloudShell availability were not tested in a live account. Test them first.

5\. Cost: 40 × t3.micro \+ 2 GiB EBS for about two hours, plus custom metrics and log ingest: a few USD in total; check current pricing. Clean-up: delete the stacks, then the alarms (created by hand).
